posts.text:
$SPCX isn't just building compute faster than every other neocloud

It has something none of them have: OPTIONALITY on every GPU it deploys

Every GW SpaceX brings online has two paths to revenue:

1. use it for Grok / xAI and capture the frontier model economics themselves, which generates more revenue than renting it out (Semianalysis estimates around $100B/GW)

2. rent it out to everyone else, at a premium

The reason SpaceX can rent out their compute at a premium is twofold:

1. Speed. SpaceX builds faster than anyone on earth, so they can get compute into customers' hands faster than any competitor. AI labs that need compute NOW pay up for that

2. The backstop. SpaceX can sign short-term contracts at higher prices because if a customer backs out, that compute simply goes to their own AI models. No empty racks, no panic

CoreWeave and Nebius can't take that risk, so they lock in most long-term deals at lower rents and fund the buildout with debt

Which brings us to funding, which is where the gap between these companies gets even wider

SpaceX doesn't have to fund the buildout (or the interest costs) from compute revenue alone. Starlink and launch cash flows can carry part of it. CoreWeave is paying 15% on unsecured bonds right now while SpaceX has diversified revenue streams across the whole company (and the best capital raiser alive running it)

And the part almost nobody is pricing in: as compute moves to space in the next few years, SpaceX owns the cheapest path to win there too. The rockets that bring the compute up AND the connectivity that beams it back down

That's why the chart above looks the way it does. Bloomberg Intelligence models SpaceX's AI ROIC going from negative 4% in 2026 to ~25% by 2030, above AWS and Google Cloud, while the pure neoclouds stay stuck in single digits

No one is better positioned to dominate the compute business in the coming years than SpaceX

This is why I still believe SpaceX is undervalued and why I've made it a core holding in my Milk Road PRO portfolio. You can see my entire real-time portfolio here: https://link.milkroad.com/t5837z

quote.author: KyleReidhead
quote.name: Kyle Reidhead | Milk Road
quote.text:
Is SpaceX competition hurting the valuation / credit risk of Neoclouds?

$CRWV and $NBIS down 10%+ today, while $SPCX down just 2% (and UP on the month)

The obvious trigger is credit risk, with CoreWeave's unsecured bonds yielding 15%

But in the last week, Elon also confirmed that SpaceX will reach 2GW by November and potentially 2.6 GW by EOY. That's .6GW ahead of schedule and quickly becoming much bigger than Coreweave and Nebius

Almost no one building compute is doing it ahead of schedule, but SpaceX is proving to be superior here on speed and is expecting close to 10GW by 2027 (And significantly more in years ahead, especially as we move to compute in Space)

At the same time, Elon also mentioned earlier this week about the difficulty in executing this build out (said even SpaceX engineers are finding it hard) but also in the ability for companies to raise capital... the issue Coreweave is having now.

But we know SpaceX and Elon has no issues in raising capital (and generating revenue from other sources too). Raising capital is what Elon excels at over anyone

So I wonder if the market is starting to see that SpaceX is becoming a very big competitor to these neoclouds, taking demand sure... though I think there is plenty of demand to go around.. but more so taking resources and capital that other neoclouds need to scale

SpaceX also has optionality to either rent out the compute or use it for xAI / Grok, which lowers risk even further to fund their compute buildout. It's also why SpaceX can charge a premium on their compute vs the other neoclouds, lowering risk even further

I'm not saying SpaceX is the full reason for Coreweaves issues, but you gotta think this evolving competitive landscape of Elon entering the ring has to have something to do with it

Even with this said, I'm still bullish on neoclouds as I think the demand remains endless, but I think SpaceX becomes the dominate neocloud by next year

quote.author: ArtificialAnlys
quote.name: Artificial Analysis
quote.text:
SpaceXAI’s Grok Voice 3.0 is the new leading Speech to Speech model, debuting at #1 on the Artificial Analysis Speech to Speech Index at 86.9, while also being competitive on latency

Grok Voice 3.0 is @SpaceXSI 's successor to Grok Voice 2.0, a Speech to Speech model available through the SpaceXAI Realtime API at $0.08 per minute. We evaluated Grok Voice 3.0 with the Rex voice through the SpaceXAI Realtime API.

Key takeaways:

➤ Speech to Speech Index: Grok Voice 3.0 debuts at #1 at 86.9, ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 83.2, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 82.6 and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 80.1. It is up on Grok Voice 2.0 at 81.3 (+5.6 points) and Grok Voice 1.0 at 73.7 (+13.2 points), released just under six months ago. The Index averages Speech Reasoning (Big Bench Audio), Agentic Performance (Tau Voice), Arena Preference, and Task Success Rate

➤ Speech Agent Arena: Grok Voice 3.0 ranks #3 in preference at Elo 1070, behind Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Minimal (1100) and Gemini 3.8 Live (1088) and ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 1057, and #1 on Task Success Rate at 94.8%, highest on the board, just ahead of Grok Voice 2.0 at 94.6%. Grok Voice 2.0 trails at Elo 1011

➤ Tau Voice: Grok Voice 3.0 takes the #2 spot on our Tau Voice benchmark implementation at 71.6%, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 74.5% and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 68.6% and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 59.3% - up from 56.5% for Grok Voice 2.0

➤ Big Bench Audio: Grok Voice 3.0 scores 98.5% on audio reasoning, ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 97.7% and Grok Voice 2.0 at 97.2%

➤ Speed: Average Time to First Audio on Big Bench Audio is 0.81 seconds for Grok Voice 3.0, well ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 1.24s, GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 1.34s and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 1.35s, though slower than Grok Voice 2.0 at 0.70s

➤ Cost: Grok Voice 3.0 costs $4.80 per hour of input audio, the same as Grok Voice 2.0. That is above GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at $4.47 and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at $3.50, cheaper than GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at $5.83, and ~2.2x cheaper than GPT-Realtime-2.1 High at $10.75

Congrats to @elonmusk  and the @SpaceXSI  team 🚀

See below for more detail ⬇️

Wokeism is the most sophisticated form of racism ever built. Not because it hates one group, but because it reduces every human being to their skin color and calls it justice.

Its roots aren't mysterious. Critical theory from the Frankfurt School, French postmodernists like Foucault and Derrida, then critical legal studies on American campuses, distilled into Critical Race Theory in the 80s and 90s. The core idea: society is nothing but a power struggle between groups. The individual doesn't exist. Merit doesn't exist. Only oppressor and oppressed.

Accept that premise and everything else follows. You're judged by your race before you open your mouth. Your success is privilege, your failure is oppression. That's not anti-racism. That's racism with a PhD.

And look at who actually holds these views. Not most minorities. Only about 3% of Hispanic Americans use "Latinx." Most Black Americans told Gallup they wanted the same or more police presence in their neighborhoods, not less. The "Hidden Tribes" study found the hard progressive activist wing is around 8% of the population, and whiter and wealthier than average. A small radicalized class speaks in the name of minorities who never asked it to.

The coalition doesn't even hold together. Feminists vs trans activists on women's sports. Asian Americans who had to go to the Supreme Court because Harvard discriminated against them in the name of diversity. A framework that keeps producing these contradictions isn't a moral philosophy. It's a hierarchy of grievances.

And none of this grew organically. It's an industry. DEI became a multi-billion dollar market: corporate trainings, consultants, foundation grants, university bureaucracies whose budgets depend on the problem never being solved. Follow the incentives and you find an entire class of people paid to see racism everywhere. Cut the money and it starts collapsing, which is exactly what we've watched since companies began slashing DEI budgets.

Real anti-racism is simple: judge people as individuals. MLK said it in 1963. Everything since that tried to replace it has been a step backwards. https://x.com/teslaownersSV/status/1884471785648972161/video/1

When Starlink became a lifeline for a family fighting to save their dad. ❤️

Nigel Norwood suffered cardiac arrest while camping at a remote beach in Western Australia, about 100 kilometres from the nearest hospital.

There was no mobile signal. His wife, Lynne, spotted another camper’s @Starlink and used it to call emergency services.

“This was the only way to get a call out from the campsite,” she later said.

While she called for help, their 16-year-old son performed CPR with another camper, and their 19-year-old son brought a nearby defibrillator. After three shocks, Nigel’s pulse returned. He received hospital care and recovered.

Starlink made that emergency call possible. When lives are at risk, a working connection can make all the difference.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.
